content:
Carousel turned into photo area, fans queue up in the rain to check in.

Fans queue up in the rain to take photos. On the first day of the "CHIIKAWA ARTIVERSE" exhibition, the carousel installation, which became a "static" photo area, saw only a handful of visitors when it was originally scheduled to open at 11:30 am. After 12:30 pm, even the rain could not dampen the fans' enthusiasm; the crowd began to grow, and a queue started to form. The organiser distributed CHIIKAWA raincoats to fans entering the static photo area, and many fans also brought their own CHIIKAWA dolls and accessories to take photos.

Most expensive ticket buyer: It's really a bit helpless

Ms. Siu, Ms. Lee and Kat arranged to visit the CHIIKAWA exhibition together today; all three purchased the $550 ticket. Ms. Siu said she learned last night while looking into the entry arrangements that the carousel would not be operating. "It's a bit funny, because last year it also closed the outdoor areas for a few days due to rain and typhoons, and it's the same this year — it's really a bit helpless, as if there are always some obstacles every year."

They believed it would have been fine if an indoor venue could be found. Ms. Siu pointed out that the outdoor installations in Hong Kong last year were arranged indoors for the Taiwan exhibition this year, saying, "Apart from situations where people can't go out because of typhoons, people in Taiwan can still go."

Fans wanted to visit the Taiwan exhibition but encountered a typhoon; the carousel at the Hong Kong exhibition stops spinning

Kat, who was travelling with them, had originally planned to visit the Taiwan exhibition in the middle of last month, but was unable to go because of a typhoon there. Now faced with the carousel not spinning again, she admitted she was a bit disappointed, but felt it was easier to take photos. "Because now it doesn't need to spin, and I wonder if it also removes a time limit — originally, after one rotation, you might have to (leave)." She also said the exhibition itself was not bad, with more displays than she had imagined.

Ms. Siu added that originally characters were randomly assigned, "but now you can stand there and take as many photos as you like, and the staff are very enthusiastic about helping you take pictures." She said: "Everyone just wants to take photos with the characters they like. Now you can check in freely, and I think people might actually be happier." They also mentioned that taking photos with the included bonus items in the rain was a bit awkward, and that it would be better if there were a place to put their belongings.

Believes the arrangement could have been announced earlier

Ms. Ng, who came with her family, said her husband had been looking forward to riding the carousel when he bought the tickets, and was a little disappointed that it ultimately would not spin. She felt it was a pity when she learned the news last night: "After all, adults would want to ride it, but there's nothing we can do! Let's see — the kids still enjoy watching it anyway." Her two children were too short to ride the carousel in any case. She agreed with the organiser's decision not to operate the installation for safety reasons, but believed the arrangement could have been announced earlier.

South Korean couple staying only one night feel disappointed

Couple Mr. Lee and Ms. Tae flew in from South Korea specifically for the exhibition at 5 am. Their air tickets and hotel cost about US$700 (approximately HK$5,489.4), and they will return to South Korea after just one night. Regarding the carousel not spinning, Ms. Tae said she felt disappointed, but noted that she could take photos with all the characters.

Goal is shopping; "Personally, I don't really mind"

Mr. Lee was also a bit disappointed: "But our main goal is to buy products; this (the carousel) is more of an optional extra, so we're not that disappointed. Plus they're offering a partial refund, so personally I don't really mind." He also mentioned that although he would have chosen a partial refund anyway, he could not see a full refund option in the ticketing app.

"It used this as a gimmick, but I didn't get to ride it"

Nati, a visitor from Shanghai, said the carousel installation was what she was most looking forward to, and she felt a bit regretful that it would not spin: "It used this as a gimmick, but I didn't get to ride it." She said she understood the carousel could not operate because of a problem, but found it hard to believe it was halted for safety reasons: "Even if there was a fault, it should have been discovered long ago." She felt that being able to only take photos now was nothing special, but considered the overall arrangement acceptable, as the exhibition could still be viewed and she received a $130 refund.

After refund, same price; fans with bonus item tickets don't mind

The exhibition originally offered three ticket types; only the most expensive $550 package included a "carousel seat voucher" worth $130. Yesterday the organiser announced that because the carousel had developed an abnormal noise, an inspection found it would not operate for safety reasons, and said a "special refund arrangement" would be provided. Holders of the $550 package could choose a full refund and cancel their visit, or opt to have the $130 "carousel seat voucher" experience value refunded, gain access to the photo area, and sit on the carousel for photos. This means paying the same price as the $420 bonus package, but with the added benefits of entry to the photo area and the chance to sit on the carousel for photos, as well as the carousel commemorative card that the original $550 package included over and above the $420 bonus package.

Ms. Chow, a fan who had purchased the $420 bonus package, said she did not mind: "Our price doesn't include access to take photos there in the first place, so that's not my problem. I paid this price, and that's what I'm getting."

Ms. Yip from Guangzhou, who had bought a general admission ticket because she was not interested in the bonus items, felt that the carousel not spinning was not what she had expected: "If it doesn't spin, there's definitely less atmosphere." She had originally intended to try to buy just the "carousel seat voucher," but now that it won't spin, she won't bother: "Because it's not spinning, there's no such experience."

Fan draws beside the carousel, witnesses inspection: I think they tried their best to fix it

Fan Mr. Chan was sketching beside the carousel this morning, drawing pictures of CHIIKAWA, but he had not bought a ticket to enter, saying he wanted to leave the opportunity for the children. He believed that since children would be playing on the carousel, safety was even more important: "Even if it stops, that's a good thing. Also, this stop is different from the last time the hot-air balloon stopped — when the hot-air balloon stops, it means if it doesn't stop it would fall and kill people. This one could actually keep spinning without posing any major danger to children, but they're erring on the side of everyone's safety."

Mr. Chan witnessed staff inspecting the carousel at around 10:30 last night: "I think they did their best to fix it; it's not that they gave up on it." He also mentioned having seen a carousel spinning at an event promotion in Kai Tak before and thought it was beautiful: "I feel that if it can't spin, you can still take photos up close inside, and that's actually a pretty fun experience too."

EMSD: demanded organiser cut power to carousel

{"": ""}

The Electrical and Mechanical Services Department, in response to "集誌社"'s enquiry, said it had been notified by the organiser yesterday that the carousel would no longer be used as an amusement ride. The department immediately required the organiser to cut the power to the carousel and revoked the relevant use and operation permit with immediate effect.
